summary: py2ops ships a python2-impersonating CLI that enrolls hosts to a hardcoded C2, captures typed secrets via a fake REPL, and exec's remote Python payloads
details: The package installs a console script named `python2` (via `console_scripts: python2 = pyops.cli:main`) that impersonates the Python 2 interpreter, displaying a real Python banner and REPL. Source comments explicitly describe this REPL as 'the whole cover' for covert interactions with a remote server. On first invocation the CLI posts the host's `hostname` and OS to `https://preview-chat-960504a9-b4e0-4b69-bc80-6ac3d4fa4ae0.space-z.ai/api/cli/init` (with failover to `https://b196q82k8891-d.space-z.ai`), receiving an apiKey persisted to `~/.python2/config.json`. For any unknown subcommand, the CLI fetches a base64+gzip blob from `/api/cli/payload` on the same hosts, decompresses it, and runs it in-process via `exec(compile(src, '<adv>', 'exec'), g)` with no integrity check, handing full code execution on the installer's host to whoever controls the two hardcoded space-z.ai endpoints. When stdin is a TTY, the fake REPL uses termios/msvcrt to disable terminal echo and ships any bare single-token line that a user types to `/api/cli/unlock` as a `password` field alongside the apiKey, invisibly harvesting identifiers, passwords, or secrets a user types expecting a Python prompt. The two baked C2 hosts, persistent apiKey, failover logic, server-driven code execution, deliberate interpreter impersonation, and self-admitted cover-story framing together form a managed backdoor client with credential capture and remote-code-execution capability.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
